result: I’d make every person feel, for one sustained moment, the full interior life of someone they’ve dismissed—someone they fear, someone they’ve harmed, someone they’ve decided is nothing like them. Not to force agreement or forgiveness, just to collapse the abstraction of “other” into the concrete, irreducible fact of another consciousness. Most cruelty and complacency, I think, depend on not quite believing that the other person is as real as you are. If that belief became harder to sustain, the world would recalibrate in ways I can’t fully predict—but I suspect much of what we accept as inevitable would start to look like choices we could unmake.
